title: The Night the Till Lied
description:
Vesper Markets closes every store at night and drops one Parquet sales file into the lake. This morning Finance opened the overnight dashboard and the totals were wrong — missing products, impossible quantities, blank discounts, currency aliases, and mixed ticket statuses had slipped into the feed.

Read that drop from `INPUT_PATH`. Apply the rules below, then write Parquet to `OUTPUT_PATH`.

The file is the Vesper overnight sales fact (15 columns). Only `product_id`, `quantity`, `discount_pct`, `currency`, and `status` need work on this lab. The other ten columns are already trusted — do not drop or rewrite them.

Use Spark DataFrame APIs. Do not `collect()` the table and loop in Python.

## Rules

Work column by column. A row is in the output only when every rule is satisfied. Values you normalize must appear that way in the written Parquet.

- **`currency`.** Treat `usd` and `$` as `USD`, `eur` as `EUR`, `gbp` as `GBP`. A missing currency is `USD`. After that, keep the row only if currency is `USD`, `EUR`, or `GBP`. `INR` is out.
- **`status`.** Treat `complete`, `Complete`, and `completed` as `COMPLETED`. Keep the row only if status is exactly `COMPLETED`. `CANCELLED` and `PENDING` are out.
- **`discount_pct`.** A missing discount is `0`.
- **`product_id`.** A missing product cannot be booked. Drop the row. Do not invent an id.
- **`quantity`.** Keep when `> 0` and `<= 100`. `100` stays. `0`, negatives, and `101+` go.

## Example

Seven input lines. Two should remain, and those two must already be normalized.

**Input**

| txn_id | product_id | quantity | discount_pct | currency | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t1 | 10 | 2 | 0.10 | USD | COMPLETED |
| t2 | *null* | 2 | 0.10 | USD | COMPLETED |
| t3 | 10 | 0 | 0.10 | USD | COMPLETED |
| t4 | 10 | 100 | *null* | usd | complete |
| t5 | 10 | 101 | 0.10 | USD | COMPLETED |
| t6 | 10 | 2 | 0.10 | INR | COMPLETED |
| t7 | 10 | 2 | 0.10 | USD | CANCELLED |

**Output** — only t1 and t4. t4’s values have changed.

| txn_id | product_id | quantity | discount_pct | currency | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t1 | 10 | 2 | 0.10 | USD | COMPLETED |
| t4 | 10 | 100 | 0 | USD | COMPLETED |

- t1 is already valid, so it is unchanged.
- t4 is kept: quantity `100` is allowed, the missing discount becomes `0`, `usd` becomes `USD`, and `complete` becomes `COMPLETED`.
- t2 is gone — no `product_id`.
- t3 is gone — quantity is `0`.
- t5 is gone — quantity is `101`.
- t6 is gone — currency is `INR`.
- t7 is gone — status is `CANCELLED`.

problemStatement.moat:
Setter notes — not shown to learners.

## What was in mind

Lab 1 of the **Vesper** overnight-sales sequence. The skill is not “drop bad rows.” It is using **`replace`, `fillna`, `dropna`, and `filter` together**, each on a different column, in that order.

Only five columns are dirty: `product_id`, `quantity`, `discount_pct`, `currency`, `status`. Everything else on the file is already good so they cannot hide a wrong transform behind noise on `store_id` / `unit_price` / ids.

The question we wanted History to answer on a failed Submit: **which of the four operations did you skip, and did you apply them in the wrong order?**

## Column → transform

| Column | Transform | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | `replace` then `fillna` then `filter` | `usd` / `$` must become `USD` before the allow-list. Null becomes `USD`. `INR` still drops. |
| `status` | `replace` then `filter` | `complete` / `Complete` / `completed` → `COMPLETED`. `CANCELLED` / `PENDING` still drop. |
| `discount_pct` | `fillna` `0` | Missing discount is 0, not a dropped sale. |
| `product_id` | `dropna` | No product → no line. Filling 0 would be a lie. |
| `quantity` | `filter` `(0, 100]` | `100` stays. `0` / negatives / `101+` go. Not repaired. |

Intended pipeline: replace → fillna → dropna → filter.

## How we created the cases

Two files only. Size is not the lesson (these are narrow column ops). 20k Run / 100k Submit is enough to look like a drop without a case matrix.

1. **`01-run-edges` (20k, Run)** — subset: null `product_id`, `quantity` 0 and 100, null `discount_pct`, `usd`, `complete`. Enough to see each transform. No `INR`, no `101`, no `CANCELLED`, no null currency.
2. **`02-submit-all` (100k, Submit)** — every kind: also negatives, `101+`, `$`, null currency, `INR`, `Complete`, `CANCELLED`, `PENDING`.

A filter-only job fails Submit: alias rows are dropped instead of repaired, null discounts stay null, null currency is gone instead of `USD`.

Trusted columns (`transaction_id`, `store_id`, `customer_id`, `unit_price`, `transaction_timestamp`) are never dirtied.

Oracle is `solution/solve.py` (same rules as `solution/src/main.py`). Grade is a row-diff on `transaction_id`, including repaired values.

## What this is not

- Not revenue (lab 2). `unit_price` is pass-through.
- Not SKU normalize (lab 3). No `product_code`.
- Not a shared `datasets/` table. Fixtures live under `challenges/l1-filter-valid-sales-rows/testcases/`.
- Not a 10-isolate matrix and not a size-of-data lab.
